ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, shareholders, and senior foreign lobbyists must be screened throughout the engagement against the UN Security Council sanctions list, the U.S. OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs unilateral sanctions list, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit suspicious transaction reporting database. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person (PEP), their family members, or close associates, including source-of-wealth verification, source-of-funds documentation, independent corroboration of business reputation, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Negative media checks, adverse regulatory history searches, corporate registries, and cross-border tax good-standing verification must be documented. All screening must be repeated at least annually and upon any change in ownership or control. The compliance file must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends, in accordance with KoFIU requirements, and made available to Korean regulatory authorities upon demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Registry of Companies / I-SAFE (Internet Search and Filing Environment) for corporate name clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the registered corporate name must be written in Hangul script. If the company uses a foreign-language trade name or the shareholder is a foreign entity, a phonetic transliteration into Hangul must be adopted and registered as the official legal name of the Korean entity. The name must follow the four-tier naming convention: (1) distinctive element identifying the entity or trade name; (2) business purpose element or descriptive words; (3) the corporate form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' or 'LLC'; and (4) any transliterated foreign-language component. The name must not be identical to any prior registered name, must not be misleading as to the company's nature, and must not contain prohibited tokens. The Korean Commercial Act and enforcement regulations require that the Hangul transliteration be a faithful phonetic representation of the foreign name, and any deviation must be justified to the registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must first obtain the written grounds of rejection from the registry, including the specific conflicting registered name or prohibited token identified. Within 30 days of the rejection decision, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the head of the relevant court of registry, attaching a comparative table of the proposed name versus the conflicting name, evidence of prior use or trademark registration, and a corrected name proposal in Hangul. The registry must review the appeal and issue a decision within a reasonable statutory period. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review through administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act. The applicant is advised to concurrently reserve a new name using the I-SAFE system to preserve any remaining reservation rights within the initial 30-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is strongly disfavored and generally rejected by Korean tax authorities and financial institutions for an active government-affairs lobbying and advisory company. Although the Korean Commercial Act does not explicitly prohibit a virtual registered address, the National Tax Service requires a fixed place of business for business registration, and banks conducting customer due diligence will expect a physical office where the directors and employees actually work, where books and records are maintained, and where regulatory inspections can be conducted. For a lobbying entity with government-audience engagement, a virtual office creates a high risk of being classified as a sham entity, triggering administrative sanctions, tax reassessment, criminal penalties for violation of the Act on External Registration of Names, or denial of corporate bank account opening. Therefore, a leased physical office in Seoul or another business district is operationally mandatory to demonstrate genuine commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Mandatory checklist for unannounced physical inspection: (1) verify that the company name plaque is displayed at the registered address; (2) confirm that the registered place of business is currently occupied and operational; (3) inspect presence of employees or a lawful representative during business hours; (4) require production of original corporate documents including business registration certificate, corporate seal, board minutes, and accounting books; (5) verify bank account statements and contracts correspond to the reported business activities; (6) confirm that lobbying engagements and advisory services are supported by written agreements and invoices; (7) ensure compliance with local zoning and building regulations. Quantified risk: for a government-affairs lobbying entity in Korea, the probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the National Tax Service or district registry office within the first 24 months of incorporation is estimated at 80%, given heightened governmental attention on policy advisory and lobbying activities. The inspection risk is materially higher than for fully virtual e-commerce businesses.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, enacted December 31, 1962, as amended, specifically Articles 543 through 583 governing Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), together with the Registration of Commercial Establishments Act and relevant provisions of the Framework Act on Civil Procedure for court registration enforcement.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Registration Division through the Internet Registration Office (IRO), with the territorial competent authority being the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office for the registered office in Seoul.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan), executed by all incorporators, notarized in Korea, and submitted together with an application for registration of incorporation under Article 549 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa under the amended Commercial Act; the amount of contribution is fixed by the Articles of Incorporation. No blocked escrow account is required by law. Capital contributions must be deposited into a Korean bank account opened by or on behalf of the incorporators, and a deposit certificate or balance confirmation from the bank must accompany the registration application. The initial contributed capital may be as low as one Korean Won, but practical bank account opening and legal formality costs require a nominal working capital amount.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDING BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY)

RECITALS
A meeting of the founding directors of Yuhan Hoesa, a Yuhan Hoesa to be incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, was duly convened at the proposed registered office on the date stated in the Articles of Incorporation. All directors entitled to vote were present either in person or by proxy, and a quorum was established. The chairperson reported that the Company is in the course of statutory incorporation and that the resolutions concern share capital subscription, banking authorization, registered office adoption, and statutory officer appointments.

RESOLUTIONS

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the total contributed capital of the Company be the amount appearing in the Articles of Incorporation, divided into units held by each incorporator; that all subscription proceeds have been deposited into a dedicated bank account established by the incorporators; and that the bank deposit certificate or balance confirmation be retained for attachment to the incorporation registration application. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors be and hereby are authorized to verify the deposit, accept the subscription releases, and issue capital contribution certificates to each member in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be the address set out in the Articles of Incorporation, situated in the jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director be and hereby is authorized to execute and deliver the registered office lease agreement, to accept service of legal process on behalf of the Company, and to file all necessary notices and registrations at such address.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company open one or more corporate bank accounts with a commercial bank licensed in Korea; that the Representative Director and the Director designated as Chief Financial Officer be appointed authorized signatories; and that all disbursements exceeding ten million Korean Won require the joint signature of the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all account opening mandates, resolution extracts, and compliance forms be executed in accordance with the Financial Transactions Reports Act and bank anti-money laundering policies.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that the persons named in the consent forms are appointed as follows: a Representative Director, a Director, and an Auditor, each to serve until the first ordinary general meeting of members or until successors are lawfully elected. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director be authorized to apply for the National Tax Service business registration certificate, to file the foreign investment notification if applicable, to engage a company seal and any required notarial certifications, and to execute all ancillary documents necessary to register the Company.

5. ADMINISTRATIVE AND GENERAL. RESOLVED, that the authorized officers and registered tax agents be instructed to file the incorporation registration with the competent District Court Registry Office, to obtain certified copies of the commercial registration record, and to complete banking, taxation, and foreign investment formalities. RESOLVED, that all actions taken by the incorporators and officers in furtherance of this formation are ratified, approved, and confirmed.

This resolution is effective as of the date of adoption and shall be recorded in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Pre-Formation Feasibility Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) and Seoul Central District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an exhaustive name search through the Internet Registration Office using the proposed Korean entity name of the Yuhan Hoesa, and verify that no identical or confusingly similar corporate name is already registered. Confirm that the proposed registered office address is physically capable of receiving civil process and is not a prohibited postal address. For ISIC 7020 government affairs advisory services, confirm that no foreign ownership restriction exists under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and that the business scope does not require a pre-approval from the National Assembly or the Financial Services Commission. All incorporators must present current passports or alien registration cards for identity verification, after which the initial draft of the Articles of Incorporation is signed for notarization scheduling. This step materially reduces the risk of correction orders at the court registration stage.
required_dossiers: Verified corporate name search output from IRO
Initial draft of the Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passports or alien registration cards of all incorporators
Proposed registered office address proof or address intent letter
Foreign investment pre-screening questionnaire if any incorporator is not a Korean national
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or confusingly similar, select a secondary name and rerun the search within one business day. If a foreign investment restriction is identified, obtain written pre-clearance from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or KOTRA before formation, or restructure the equity ownership to remove the restricted attribute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Deposit and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean notary public and a Korean commercial bank supervised by the Financial Supervisory Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital deposit account at a Korean bank using the incorporator identification documents. Transfer the agreed paid-up capital amount into that account and request a bank certificate of deposit or balance confirmation that clearly states the depositor name, the account number, and the deposited amount. After the deposit is verified, all incorporators must appear before a licensed Korean notary public for execution and authentication of the Articles of Incorporation. The notary will verify legal capacity, confirm that the Articles contain all mandatory statements, and certify the deed. Each appointed director and auditor must sign a separate consent to appointment form. The original notarized Articles are then retained for submission to the court registry. This step must be completed within the recommended statutory preparation window before the two-week filing deadline.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of deposit or balance confirmation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Signed consent to appointment forms of directors and auditor
Power of attorney in Korean if an incorporator is represented by an agent
Corporate registration certificate and corporate resolution if an incorporator is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate lacks a bank seal or ledger signature, request a reissued confirmation. If the notary identifies a legal defect in the Articles, revise the defective clause and re-execute the Articles before the same notary; no new capital deposit is required if the funds remain unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration Filing with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registry Office or the local district court registry Office for the registered office, accessible electronically through the Supreme Court IRO portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the competent District Court Registry through the Internet Registration Office or by in-person submission at the designated civil registry window. The application must be signed by the Representative Director and accompanied by the original notarized Articles of Incorporation, director and auditor consent forms, the bank capital deposit certificate, and proof of payment of court registration tax. The registry clerk will verify compliance with Commercial Act Articles 543 through 583 and with the Registration of Commercial Establishments Act. Upon approval, the commercial register entry is completed, the certificate of registered matters is issued, and the legal existence of the Yuhan Hoesa becomes effective. After issuance, obtain a certified copy of the registered matters containing the unique company registration number and corporate identity information for subsequent banking and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration application form signed by the Representative Director
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Director and auditor consent to appointment forms
Bank capital deposit certificate or balance confirmation
Receipt or payment confirmation for court registration tax
Power of attorney if filing is made by a licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure the stated omission or defect within fourteen calendar days and refile without a new statutory fee. If the application is refused, obtain the written refusal grounds, engage a Korean licensed attorney, and either file an appeal or submit a corrected application within a fresh registration window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Tax Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the Home Tax Service portal or the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the incorporation registration, or before actual business commencement if earlier, apply for the business registration certificate under Article 168 of the Income Tax Act and Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act. The application must state the corporate legal name, registration number, registered office, representative director, business purpose, phone number, and expected tax invoice contact. Attach the certified copy of the commercial registration record and the lease contract for the registered office. After the tax official verifies the information, the NTS issues the business registration certificate and assigns a unique business registration number. This certificate is mandatory for opening the operating bank account and for issuing lawful electronic tax invoices under the Value-Added Tax Act. For a government affairs and lobbying advisory company, select the consulting business tax code and register the entity as a general business taxpayer for VAT purposes.
required_dossiers: Prescribed NTS business registration application form
Certified copy of the commercial registration record
Lease contract or certified building owner consent for the registered office
Representative director identification and resident registration or foreign registration number
Corporate seal certificate if a seal is registered
Tax agent power of attorney in Korean if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS returns the application as incomplete, correct the business classification code or registered address on the Home Tax Service portal and resubmit. If the tax office requests additional landlord verification, submit a certified rent payment ledger or an owner confirmation. Any late-filing administrative surcharge is limited to statutory amounts and may be mitigated by voluntary disclosure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Activation and Post-Incorporation Regulatory Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission, Financial Intelligence Unit, and KOTRA or a foreign exchange bank for foreign investment notification matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business registration certificate is issued, execute the banking resolution by opening the permanent corporate operating account. Present the certified copy of the commercial registration, business registration certificate, representative director passport, lease agreement, first board resolution appointing signatories, and the corporate seal certificate if one has been made. The bank will perform customer due diligence and, for a medium-risk retainer-based government affairs advisory firm, may require an enhanced beneficial ownership declaration and source of funds evidence. If any incorporator is a foreign person, file the foreign investment notification through KOTRA or a licensed foreign exchange bank before remitting capital, or within five business days after receipt, and retain the foreign investment certificate. Finally, implement an internal anti-bribery and anti-corruption compliance manual aligned with the Act on the Prevention of Corruption and Bribery, and confirm that office-only activities do not trigger an industrial permit, environmental permit, or civil defense fire license at the company level.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account application package and resolution extract
National Tax Service business registration certificate
Certified copy of commercial registration record
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution
KYC and AML forms with ultimate beneficial owner declaration
Lease agreement and building owner fire safety certificate
Foreign investment notification form and receipt if foreign investment applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank escalates the KYC review, supply an audited source-of-funds statement or a law-firm beneficial owner confirmation and resubmit. If the foreign investment notification is late, file a voluntary late notification with KOTRA or the exchange bank and pay any administrative surcharge. If the landlord cannot produce a fire safety certificate, request a temporary building safety compliance document from the building manager before finalizing the lease.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the municipal industrial licensing bureau do not require an industrial establishment license for a pure government affairs, trade policy analysis, and lobbying advisory company under ISIC 7020 (Business and Management Consulting Activities); no factory establishment, assembly line, chemical plant, or warehouse permit is triggered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable as an industrial operating permit. The active operating authorizations required are only the National Tax Service business registration certificate, and, if applicable, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification certificate; no manufacturing or physical operating license is required for an office-based consulting and lobbying activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Environment and the Seoul Metropolitan Government environmental bureau have no EIA jurisdiction over an office-based consulting service with zero physical effluent discharge, zero large combustion source, and no on-site hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the project does not constitute a development of an area or operation of a manufacturing facility that would trigger a Full Environmental Impact Assessment, a Prior Environmental Review, or a Small-Scale Environmental Consultation under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there are no wastewater discharge points, volatile organic compound emission stacks, particulate emission sources, or hazardous waste generation streams. Ordinary office waste is managed through municipal waste collection contracts under the Wastes Control Act, and workplace office appliances must comply with the Energy Efficiency Labeling and Standards Act only to the extent applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at the company license level for a pure office-based consulting and lobbying entity. The building owner must maintain a completed fire protection inspection and civil defense fire safety approval under the Framework Act on Fire-Fighting Services, and the lessee must pass an ordinary workplace safety review under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. For offices with fewer than the statutory threshold of workers and with no hazardous equipment, no separate KOSHA registration or civil defense fire permit is required; the company should retain the landlord fire safety certificate and conduct a basic ergonomic and electrical safety checklist for compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS); electronic filing portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr). Export clearances and customs declarations are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS (https://unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine Korean tax presence. If the foreign non-resident entity has a domestic place of business in Korea, it is treated as a foreign corporation with a Korean business establishment and must file a business registration application with the district tax office having jurisdiction. Step 2: Appoint a Korean tax representative who is jointly liable for tax filing and payment, or an authorized agent through a valid power of attorney. Step 3: File the Foreign Business Registration application with the responsible district tax office or via HomeTax, attaching the foreign certificate of incorporation (translated and, where required, apostilled), articles of association, proof of the Korean place of business such as a lease agreement, the tax representatives identification, and the power of attorney. Step 4: The NTS reviews the application and issues the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the entity TIN and VAT registration number under the Value-Added Tax Act. A foreign non-resident entity with no Korean domestic place of business but supplying taxable services, including imported electronic/digital services, in Korea must also register for VAT through a court-authorized tax representative before the first taxable supply under Article 53 of the Value-Added Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for U.S.-style check-the-box or elective pass-through classification. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act on its worldwide income. The only relevant statutory election is the domestic consolidated corporate tax return regime available to a qualifying parent-subsidiary group with 100% domestic ownership, subject to NTS approval. Hybrid mismatch treatment is mandatory rather than elective under Korea's implementation of the OECD hybrid mismatch rules; no special hybrid election mechanism is available for a government-affairs lobbying advisory entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, administered by the National Tax Service
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A - no general turnover-based VAT registration threshold; every business operator, including a foreign non-resident operator supplying VAT-liable services in Korea, must register within 20 days of commencement of a taxable business. A simplified taxable person threshold of KRW 80 million in annual revenue applies only to certain small individual proprietors and is a compliance simplification, not a registration exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory under the Value-Added Tax Act; all VAT-registered business operators must issue tax invoices, and businesses above the statutory e-tax invoice threshold, or those requested by a counterparty, must issue electronic tax invoices through HomeTax or an approved EDI/API service provider. E-tax invoice details are transmitted to the NTS at issuance, after which the NTS assigns a national e-tax invoice serial number and automatically cross-matches the data against VAT returns, customs declarations, and corporate income tax records. Korea does not use a physical fiscal stamp or digital stamp device; anti-fraud integrity is achieved through near-real-time e-invoice clearance, mandatory electronic transmission, third-party data matching with the Korea Customs Service and foreign exchange banks, and penalties for failure to transmit or for issuing false e-tax invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, goods are zero-rated when physically exported from Korea under a customs export declaration, and services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident or foreign place of business, used or consumed outside Korea, and paid for from abroad with foreign currency. For the Yuhan Hoesa cross-border government-affairs advisory and lobbying-consulting services, the services must be supplied to a non-resident beneficiary, the actual performance and benefit must occur outside Korea, and the consideration must be received through the Korean foreign exchange banking system. Qualifying offshore digital services, such as online policy research, digital advisory deliverables, or electronic data-analytics reports, may also be zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient and the place of use is demonstrably outside Korea; the taxpayer must retain evidence of the recipient's non-resident status, foreign place of use, and foreign-currency inward remittance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate) issued by the Korea Customs Service showing the exporter, consignee, HS code, quantity, and FOB value
Commercial Invoice and Packing List signed by the exporter
Bill of Lading for sea freight, Air Waybill for air freight, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from Korea
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice issued under the Value-Added Tax Act referencing the 0% VAT rate and the statutory zero-rating provision
Foreign Currency Receipt Certificate or Foreign Exchange Remittance Confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank proving collection of export proceeds
For service exports: written advisory contract, service delivery report, and documentation demonstrating the recipient is a non-resident and the place of use or benefit is outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Korea Customs Service and the National Tax Service jointly audit zero-rated export claims by cross-matching customs export declarations, e-tax invoice transmissions, and foreign exchange bank remittance records. If the required documentation is missing, inconsistent, or untimely, or if export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day deadline (or the approved extended deadline), the zero-rating is revoked retroactively and the NTS assesses output VAT at 10% on the gross export consideration for the relevant VAT return period. Additional penalty taxes are imposed for late or non-filed returns, understated taxable amounts, and failure to issue a valid zero-rated e-tax invoice. In cases of fraudulent false tax invoices, false export declarations, or fraudulent foreign-exchange documentation, criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Value-Added Tax Act apply, including imprisonment and fines, and the NTS may pursue retrospective clawbacks for all periods within the statutory tax assessment window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and Korea Customs Service under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and associated Regulations on Foreign Exchange Transactions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but supervision-heavy foreign exchange regime. The Korean won is fully convertible on the current account for genuine trade, service fees, and profit remittances after tax clearance, while capital account transactions are generally permissible if reported to a foreign exchange bank or the Bank of Korea. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds; exporters may retain earnings in Foreign Currency Accounts. However, certain restitution and reporting obligations apply: equity injections require advance filing under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and inbound remittances above USD 50,000 must pass through an authorized foreign exchange bank with stated purpose codes. Dividends and branch profits may be repatriated after audited financial statements and withholding tax settlement, subject to the foreign investor registration certificate. Non-resident shareholders engaging in government affairs or lobbying activities will attract enhanced scrutiny because the underlying business is politically sensitive. Practical convertibility risk arises at the clearing level: KRW is an onshore currency with no offshore window, so any offshore counterparty must convert through an authorized dealer. The Bank of Korea monitors large or unusual transactions and may request underlying contract evidence before an exchange bank releases settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current Korean foreign exchange regulations, exporters are not required to convert foreign currency export proceeds into KRW; the statutory surrender ratio is 0%. However, the exporter must obtain receipt of the foreign exchange within the contractually agreed settlement date and, where the period is not agreed, within one year of the export declaration date for goods or service completion date for services. Any delayed receipts must be reported to the designated foreign exchange bank through a Delayed Receipt of Export Proceeds report, and amounts exceeding USD 50,000 per transaction need full supporting documentation such as bill of lading, commercial invoice, service contract, or a retained advisory agreement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for any offshore digital EMI acting as the primary treasury or clearing rail. Under the Banking Act and Electronic Financial Transactions Act, only institutions licensed by the Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service may receive deposits and provide foreign exchange services in the Korean jurisdiction. Foreign EMIs such as Revolut or Wise are not licensed as Korean banks, cannot issue local IBANs denominated in KRW, and cannot provide the required Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting or capital verification certificates. Such EMIs may be used only as a pre-funded supplementary payment gateway after a compliant bank account is established, never as the main account for inbound equity, outbound trade, or FX hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory representative or an authorized local signatory must complete an in-branch interview at the chosen Tier-1 Korean bank. Pure remote consular proxy opening is not generally available for a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa; however, a foreign director may execute a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney naming a locally resident officer, and the local officer must appear physically with the original POA, the company seal, and corporate resolutions. Some banks will permit a video-conference KYC interview only after the POA holder has been physically identified and the board resolution approved by the compliance committee. Enhanced due diligence will require verification of the ultimate beneficial owners of any holding company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk cross-border ownership structure with non-resident UBOs and opaque intermediate holding jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract for every entity layer; complete UBO declaration using the bank-prescribed form; valid passport and residence proof for each beneficial owner; notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation; articles of association; three years of audited financial statements for foreign shareholders; recent original bank statements from the remitting shareholder account; a clear source-of-funds narrative and the underlying cross-border advisory contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Government affairs and lobbying business scope creates perceived corruption, PEP, and foreign-influence underwriting risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Korean business license for ISIC 7020 advisory services; government-relations consultancy registration or applicable trade ministry filing; operational and compliance manual prohibiting bribery of public officials; PEP and sanctions screening files for every counterparty and public sector principal; a complete list of intended engagements with executive agencies and the National Assembly; third-party anti-corruption certification; and senior management acknowledgement of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and Korean anti-bribery statutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical substance in Korea with a nominee director or purely external management
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dated and registered Korean office lease agreement; payroll and social security records for local employees or retained local compliance officer; board resolution delegating banking authority and compliance oversight; entity opening certificate with apostille; tax office notice of incorporation; a monthly transaction forecast; proof that the Yuhan Hoesa maintains actual books and records in Korea; and a declaration issued by the local compliance officer describing the business operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity remittance from foreign shareholders whose funds are tied to government retainers and political-adjacent clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved Foreign Investment Report certificate or KOTRA filing reference; remittance purpose specifically marked as foreign direct investment and paid-in capital; bank reference letters from the remitting bank; audited ultimate parent group accounts; fully executed retainer contracts between the Yuhan Hoesa and each government-related client; sanctions and adverse-media screening reports; and the foreign investor registration certificate issued after capital verification by the receiving Korean bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound equity, the foreign investor must first submit a foreign investment report through the chosen foreign exchange bank or KOTRA before the remittance is transmitted. The shareholder shall send a SWIFT MT103 wire from a compliant banking jurisdiction to the Yuhan Hoesa capital escrow account held at the designated Korean Tier-1 bank, with the purpose code and narrative clearly stating Foreign Direct Investment, paid-in capital, and the Korean Entity registration identification. The receiving bank will evidence the remittance and issue a Certificate of Import of Foreign Capital, which supports the capital verification process and the subsequent foreign investment registration certificate. Any mismatch in remitter name, beneficiary name, amount, or purpose code will trigger mandatory BOK reporting and may cause automatic escrow blocking until the Lawful Source of Funds dossier is presented.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should be paid via SWIFT MT103 for pure retainer settlements and cross-border professional fees, with invoice, contract, and purpose code retained on file. For goods-backed transactions, a commercial letter of credit opened through a Korean foreign exchange bank via SWIFT MT700 and confirmed by a second bank is the strongest clearing rail; documentary collections may be used using D/P or D/A terms with the presenting bank receiving MT400 payment instructions. Domestic KRW transfers are cleared using KFTC and BOK-Wire+, while cross-border remittances use the USD or EUR correspondent network because KRW cannot be freely settled offshore. All outbound payments require underlying evidence and must be reported to the designated bank for BOK statistical and supervision purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with an authorized Korean dealer bank, limited to documented trade, service, or investment exposure
Onshore cross-currency swaps matching foreign currency debt or equity capital flows, subject to BOK and foreign exchange bank approval

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for non-resident counterparties hedging KRW exposure, or for domestic entities where the onshore bank provides NDF execution with clear proof of economic underlying
FX options on a cost-hedging basis only, prohibited for speculative uncovered positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Final Return and Attached Tax-Basis Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three calendar months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end Yuhan Hoesa, filing is due no later than 31 March of the immediately following fiscal year, unless a statutory one-month extension has been granted by the competent tax office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A non-filing surtax of 20 percent of the assessed corporate income tax is imposed; an unjustified under-reporting surtax of 20 percent, or 40 percent where the concealment is intentional or materially dishonest, is imposed on the unreported tax base. The unpaid tax bears statutory arrears interest calculated daily under the National Tax Collection Act, and continuous delinquency can result in tax seizure, compulsory execution, closure of the business identification number, and judicial application for administrative dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (municipal, county, or district tax authority) through the WeTax or local e-tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The local income tax surcharge is reported and paid simultaneously with the corporate income tax final return; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the deadline is 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing and underreporting penalties under the Framework Act on Local Taxes mirror the national tax surtax regime, generally 20 percent of unpaid local tax. Overdue local tax accrues daily local arrears charges, and prolonged non-payment permits municipal seizure and a request to cancel the business registration or strike off the legal entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Profit or Loss Appropriation Approval by Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The members of the Yuhan Hoesa acting at the annual members meeting, with the executed resolution placed in the corporate minute book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The members must approve the annual financial statements within three months after the close of each fiscal year, i.e., by 31 March for a 31 December year-end; if a statutory audit applies, the independent auditor report is attached before approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing penalty is levied on a non-audited Yuhan Hoesa for delayed internal approval, but directors may not lawfully declare distributions until approval is given. In tax and bank audits, absence of a signed members resolution may cause expense disallowances, reclassification of distributions, exposure to Commercial Act fines, and an administrative strike-off risk if the company repeatedly fails to satisfy statutory books and records requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent Certified Public Auditor Report and Financial Supervisory Service Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the external audit information filing system, and the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants for workpaper inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: This obligation applies only if the Yuhan Hoesa crosses a compulsory audit threshold. The independent Korean certified public auditor must complete the audit within 120 days after fiscal year-end, and the audited statements and auditor report must be filed with the FSS within 15 days after the report date; for a 31 December year-end, the practical FSS filing deadline is approximately mid-May of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor within the statutory deadline triggers a designated-auditor procedure by the Financial Services Commission and a penalty of up to KRW 50 million. Submission of a false or non-compliant audit report, or failure to file the audit report, may lead to criminal fines, publication of the sanction, automatic restriction under tax and foreign investment regimes, and, in severe cases, administrative dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investor and Beneficial Ownership Change Report, including Annual AML Client Due Diligence Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the integrated foreign investment information system, and the Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) for suspicious transaction reports
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Korea does not operate a central annual UBO return for a private Yuhan Hoesa. The company must update the Register of Members immediately on any ownership transfer and align the ownership schedule in the next annual corporate tax return. A foreign investor must file the acquisition or transfer report with KOTRA or MOTIE within 30 days before or after closing. Client due diligence for the government-affairs advisory business must be refreshed at least annually, and any suspicious transaction involving a foreign public official must be reported to KoFIU within three business days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to record a member or to deliver the required KOTRA report can expose the Yuhan Hoesa and its directors to statutory fines of up to KRW 5 million per instance. Wilful non-reporting to KoFIU under the Financial Transaction Reports Act is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment and substantial fines. Persistent compliance failure may result in licence revocation for the ISIC 7020 government-affairs advisory activity and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Registers Audit and Corporate Secretary Compliance Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Managing director or appointed corporate secretary, evidenced by a signed compliance certificate placed in the minute book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per fiscal year, normally performed immediately after the annual financial statement approval by members; for a 31 December year-end, the register audit and certificate are completed by 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: This is an internally verifiable governance obligation. Missing or inaccurate statutory registers constitute a regulatory breach in tax and reference audits and expose directors to statutory fines under the Commercial Act. A clean register certificate is customarily required by foreign counterparties, banks, and trade-policy licensing authorities; failure to produce it may impair the entity's good standing and trigger administrative strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies of the Republic of Korea, a Yuhan Hoesa must be audited by an independent certified public accountant if: (a) its total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year reach KRW 12 billion or more, approximately USD 8.9 million at an illustrative exchange rate of KRW 1,350 to USD 1.00; (b) its annual turnover from ISIC 7020 government-affairs, trade-policy analysis, and foreign-stakeholder lobbying services reaches KRW 10 billion or more and it is not classified as a small or medium enterprise under the Framework Act on SMEs; (c) it employs more than 300 full-time equivalent persons on foreign stakeholder advisory work and has total assets of at least KRW 5 billion; or (d) the Financial Services Commission or the competent licensing ministry designates the company as a public-interest or publicly significant auditee because its government-affairs advice to foreign stakeholders affects Korean trade policy. Separate financial-sector or AML regulations may also require audited financial statements if the company becomes a regulated adviser for public-interest clients.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared using Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) if the Yuhan Hoesa is in the mandatory audit category or is a public-interest entity; otherwise, Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) and the applicable accounting standards for small and medium enterprises apply. The tax-basis financial statements attached to the National Tax Service return are reconciled from these accounting records under the Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require a private Yuhan Hoesa to file a standalone annual beneficial ownership return. Instead, the Commercial Act requires continuous accuracy of the Register of Members and immediate entry of transfers; the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires a report to KOTRA or MOTIE within 30 days of any foreign investor acquisition or transfer of ownership interests, including each change of beneficial ownership linked to a foreign public authority or state fund. The Yuhan Hoesa must also keep in its registered files a signed annual confirmation by the managing director identifying every member and actual controller as of the fiscal year-end, and must refresh AML client due diligence annually because the ISIC 7020 business is classified as medium-risk enhanced for government-relations advisory work.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600 to US$3,500 per year for a Seoul or Gyeonggi registered-office agreement with corporate secretarial support and annual register-keeping for a small or medium Yuhan Hoesa.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000 to US$25,000 per year for a typical statutory audit of a Yuhan Hoesa with moderate cross-border government-affairs revenue, depending on transaction complexity, number of foreign shareholders, and K-IFRS or K-GAAP conversion requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200,000,000; 19% on taxable income between KRW 200,000,001 and KRW 20,000,000,000; 21% on taxable income exceeding KRW 20,000,000,000; plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate income tax, producing effective marginal rates of approximately 9.9%, 20.9% and 23.1%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones may obtain a 100% corporate tax exemption for 5 years and a 50% reduction for a further 2 years under the Tax Incentive Limitation Law. R&D expenses benefit from an additional income tax deduction of up to 25% to 50% of qualifying R&D expenditures, and qualified Korean-source technology transfer income may be exempt from corporate income tax under the technology income deduction provisions. Foreign tax credits are available for taxes paid by a Korean domestic corporation on its foreign-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return on Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement filed under Article 60 of the Corporate Income Tax Act; portal is the National Tax Service electronic filing system HomeTax at www.hometax.go.kr; supplementary transfer pricing schedules and local income tax schedules are filed with the same return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a provisional semi-annual corporate income tax prepayment is due within 2 months after the first 6 months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a Yuhan Hoesa with a December 31 fiscal year-end, the statutory filing deadline is March 31 of the following year. If audited financial statements are certified by an independent external auditor under the Act on External Audit, the deadline may be extended by one month to April 30 upon written request to the tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identification and Tax Residence Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate name, business registration number, corporate income tax number, responsible tax office, address of head office, fiscal year period, ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541820 industry classification, entity type as Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), and particulars of all shareholders and representatives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare each non-resident shareholder holding at least 5% of the equity interests, identify foreign parents and affiliates, and confirm that central management and control is exercised by the board in Korea. If board decisions are made outside Korea or the company has no physical office or staff in Korea, the National Tax Service may assert that the entity is a treaty-shopping shell or that it has a foreign place of effective management; attach the corporate constitution, board resolution register and lease/employee records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue, cost of services rendered, gross profit, selling and administrative expenses, operating income, non-operating income and expenses, pretax net income, total assets and total equity as shown in the statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Government affairs and lobbying retainer revenue from foreign principals must be recognized on an accrual basis and supported by executed service agreements and delivery records. Cash receipts, wire transfers and operating bank accounts must be traceable to the books. Any payments received without documentary proof of services should be separately disclosed and recharacterized as non-taxable contribution or risk receiving anti-fraud review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable Adjustments and Non-Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of permanent differences and temporary differences: entertainment expense limits, non-deductible donations, fines and penalties, depreciation, bad debt reserves, provisions, and special adjustments required by the Corporate Income Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees paid to foreign related parties for management consulting, policy analysis, public affairs or lobbying support are non-deductible unless the taxpayer proves that the services were actually rendered, were not duplicative of local services, and produced economic benefits to the Korean entity. Expenses related to gifts and entertainment of domestic or foreign public officials are subject to the Improper Solicitation and Graft Act and may be wholly denied; they must not be buried in general consulting expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Base Computation, Loss Carryforward and Exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all positive and negative adjustments, application of available net operating loss carryforwards, tax-exempt income, foreign dividend exemption, special deductions and itemized incentive deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A domestic Yuhan Hoesa reports worldwide income. Loss carryforwards may offset taxable income for up to 10 years. If the entity is treated as a domestic corporation, foreign branch income and foreign-source dividends may be exempt under the foreign dividend exemption rules if the 25% shareholding and holding-period requirements are satisfied; non-resident shareholders should not confuse the entity-level tax return with their personal or parent company tax returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - National Tax Computation, Credits and Local Income Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the tiered national corporate income tax rates, computation of the 10% local income tax surcharge, interim prepayment credits, withholding tax credits, foreign tax credit, R&D tax credits and any free-zone tax holiday calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit cannot exceed the Korean corporate income tax attributable to the same foreign source income. A foreign parent cannot use its own foreign tax credits in the Korean LLC return. The local income tax surcharge is calculated as an additional 10% of the national corporate tax payable and is due with the same return; failure to compute local income tax creates a separate delinquency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Intercompany Transactions and Transfer Pricing Presentation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of all controlled transactions with foreign related parties, including services, management fees, royalties, interest, retainers and subsidies; foreign related-party names, tax residence, transaction amounts, transfer pricing methods, comparability adjustments and any bilateral or unilateral advance pricing arrangement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the aggregate intercompany transactions with foreign related parties equal or exceed KRW 50,000,000,000, the Master File and Local File must be attached. MNE groups with prior fiscal year consolidated revenue of KRW 100,000,000,000 or more must file a CbC report notification. For government-affairs and lobbying retainers, the fees must be benchmarked under the arm's length standard; a fee based solely on a percentage of government contract value is not arm's length and may be recharacterized as a prohibited contingent lobbying fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Non-Resident Withholding and DTA Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record of dividends, interest and royalties paid to non-residents, national withholding tax computation, treaty rate claimed, Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement, and the application for reduced withholding under a bilateral income tax treaty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold 20% national tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge on outbound dividend, interest and royalty payments, an effective aggregate rate of 22%, unless the payee files a complete DTA relief application with the withholding agent before the payment date. A foreign parent claiming a 10% treaty rate must be the true beneficial owner and must provide a TRC, substance evidence and a limitation-on-benefits declaration; if documentation is missing, withhold 22% and permit a refund claim through the National Tax Service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Supplementary Disclosure and Anti-Avoidance Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: External auditor certification, aggregate financial statements, special tax zone declarations, public sector client details, AML/KYC information, beneficial ownership identifiers and any transactions involving foreign public officials.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ultimate beneficial owners must be disclosed even if the registered shareholders are nominee companies. Payments to foreign public officials or government decision-makers must be declared for anti-bribery review; undisclosed ownership structures will be referred to the Financial Intelligence Unit and may trigger a travel ban and blacklisting of the responsible director.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax; if no tax is payable, the additional tax is 0.5% of the tax base. Under-declaration of income attracts 10% additional tax, but unlawful or deliberately fraudulent omission of income attracts 40%. Delayed payment of the assessed tax accrues statutory delayed-payment interest at approximately 10.95% per annum, adjusted quarterly, and the local income tax surcharge is separately demanded. False returns can be prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to 3 times the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on outbound dividends paid to non-resident shareholders under Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national withholding tax, resulting in an effective aggregate withholding rate of 22%, unless reduced by an applicable bilateral Double Tax Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must file an application for exemption from or reduction of withholding tax with the National Tax Service through the Korean withholding agent before the payment date. The mandatory packet includes: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction covering the year of payment; (2) a Beneficial Ownership certificate and declaration confirming that the recipient owns the income, is not acting as a nominee or conduit, and will not pass the income through to a person ineligible for benefits; (3) the DTA-specific limitation-on-benefits questionnaire where applicable; and (4) a board resolution and payment agreement evidencing the economic substance of the underlying cross-border transaction. The withholding agent must conduct a reasonable care review and keep all documentation for at least 5 years; if the application is incomplete, the statutory 22% rate must be withheld and the non-resident must apply for a refund later through a Korean tax representative.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Korean withholding tax on outbound interest and royalties to non-residents is 20% national tax plus 10% local surcharge, an effective 22%. Under most Korean OECD-compliant DTAs, the treaty rate for industrial royalties and arm's length interest is 10% of the gross amount, and dividends are generally reduced to 10% where the recipient is a company owning at least 25% of the capital, with 15% in the ordinary portfolio case and the exact rate depending on the specific treaty text; all treaty benefits are denied where the beneficiary maintains a permanent establishment in Korea to which the income is effectively connected.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50,000,000,000 of aggregate cross-border transactions with foreign related parties in the fiscal year triggers compulsory Master File and Local File preparation and filing with the annual corporate income tax return; MNE groups with prior-year consolidated revenue of KRW 100,000,000,000 or more are also required to file a CbC report notification. The annual corporate tax return must attach a related-party transaction summary for all controlled cross-border service, interest, royalty and intercompany financing transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime in the form of certain Middle Eastern offshore jurisdictions, but the substance-over-form doctrine is codified through the place of effective management test, general anti-avoidance rules, controlled foreign company rules and treaty limitation-on-benefits clauses. For a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in government affairs and lobbying, the National Tax Service will examine whether the Core Income-Generating Activities are performed by actual employees in Korea, whether the entity controls its bank accounts, maintains a physical office, pays Korean employment taxes, and makes independent business decisions; a merely immigrant-taxed shell without real economic presence will be denied DTA benefits and may be recharacterized as a permanent establishment of the foreign parent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of retained government affairs income from foreign principals, fabrication of deductible lobbying consultancy expenses, use of an unreported foreign bank account, or deliberate concealment of revenue and outbound income distributions in the Yuhan Hoesa corporate income tax return with intent to evade national corporate income tax and the 10% local income tax surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax; under the Corporate Income Tax Act, unlawful omission triggers an additional tax of 40% of the unreported amount, failure to file triggers 20% of the unpaid tax, and under-declaration triggers 10%; the National Tax Service may immediately assess the tax, seize bank accounts and cancel business registrations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the director transfers corporate assets into personal accounts, uses the LLC as a mere fraud instrument, or is the de facto controlling person: the director may be held secondarily liable under the National Tax Collection Act, may have personal assets attached, may be placed on the NTS customs/immigration blacklist with a travel ban, and may face imprisonment up to 5 years; civil restitution is ordered for the full amount of evaded tax plus interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering, Foreign Exchange Violation and Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Yuhan Hoesa as a shell pass-through to receive retainer wire transfers from foreign principals and immediately disburse them to Korean public officials or related parties, failing to declare foreign exchange receipt of funds under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, or maintaining circular invoicing through an empty overseas lobbying company to create artificial deductions and to conceal the non-resident ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalizes unregistered foreign exchange brokerage and undeclared inbound payments with fines up to KRW 50,000,000 and imprisonment; the Financial Transaction Reports Act requires suspicious transactions above KRW 10,000,000 to be reported, and failure can lead to criminal penalties and asset freezing orders; the Anti-Money Laundering authorities may issue a freezing order on the corporate bank account and revoke the entity's foreign direct investment registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who personally directs the shell arrangement is civilly liable for fraudulent conveyance and restitution of all illicit flows; personal bank accounts are subject to freeze orders, the director is placed on international travel blacklists, and criminal imprisonment up to 3 years applies under the AML framework; if corporate assets are insufficient, the court may attach the director's personal property under the alter ego doctrine recognized in Korean civil execution practice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Fatal DTA Treaty-Shopping Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and attach the statutory Master File and Local File for intercompany transactions exceeding KRW 50,000,000,000, or charging the Korean LLC for government affairs lobbying fees without demonstrating actual services, economic substance, or an arm's length benchmark; simultaneously claiming a treaty-reduced withholding rate on dividends, interest or royalties through a related foreign holding entity that is not the true beneficial owner and has no substantive business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Tax Adjustment Act, the National Tax Service may make a transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's length amount, impose a 30% international tax adjustment penalty on the adjusted understated tax base, disallow all treaty benefits under the anti-avoidance and principal purpose provisions, and calculate delayed-payment interest at the statutory rate; the Corporate Income Tax Act additionally allows correction assessments with additional taxes of 20-40% for false or unjust returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signs false transfer pricing schedules and DTA certificates may be personally assessed for penalties where the limited liability company is used as a mere tool for tax avoidance; the director faces secondary tax collection, asset seizure, blacklisting by customs, immigration and public procurement agencies, travel restrictions, and criminal prosecution for producing false official documents, with imprisonment up to 5 years if the transfer pricing adjustment is accompanied by fabricated invoices, back-dated agreements or inflated royalty payments.
